title: Topological sort
learn: DAGs, Kahn's algorithm (in-degree BFS), DFS-based order, cycle detection in directed graphs
hook: Course Schedule I and II are asked all the time: "can you finish all courses" and "in what order". Topological sort is the answer, and it doubles as cycle detection for directed graphs.

explain.prompt: Explain topological sort with Kahn's algorithm and how it tells you whether the courses can all be finished.
keyPoints: directed edge pre → course means pre must come first
compute in-degrees; start a queue with every node of in-degree 0
pop a node, append it to the order, decrement its neighbours' in-degrees and queue those that reach 0
if the order contains all V nodes it's valid; otherwise the leftovers are in a cycle
